newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel little changed vs dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel little changed vs dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed almost unchanged against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Tuesday in dull trading, dealers said.
"Trading continues to be extremely quiet and the shekel was stable and trendless during the whole day," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.
"We saw slightly more conversions of shekels into dollars and the bank of Israel had to intervene on a relatively low scale buying $50 to $100 million," he said.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to support the currency basket, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for three months.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.4100 shekels against 3.4110 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6825 shekels against 3.6815 on Monday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7090 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.6964 on Monday, and against the mark at 1.9714 shekels compared with 1.9744 on Monday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.4090 shekels.
